note: Chapter 1 dialogue. id, speaker, line, emotion (neutral/dry/warm/angry/afraid/tired/amused/sad/tense). Original writing.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Easy. Smell that? River. We'll have water tonight, and maybe a roof.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Eighteen months, Tom. Four names. One town at a time.

lines.speaker: newsboy
lines.line: Lantern! Port Linden Lantern! Syndicate offers four dollars the acre! Four dollars for river land!

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Four dollars. Somebody's getting robbed, and it ain't the syndicate.

lines.speaker: stablehand
lines.line: Two bits the night, ma'am, oats extra. She's a fine one. What do you call her?

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Depends on her mood. Today she's Patience.

lines.speaker: tough1
lines.line: Old man's already half dead. Let's call it a whole and be home for supper.

lines.speaker: tough2
lines.line: Mister Shale said no talkers. Swede talks. Swedes always talk.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Evening. Did I hear the name Shale?

lines.speaker: tough1
lines.line: You heard wrong, lady. Ride on, while riding's still something you can do.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I've been riding on a long while. Think I'll stop here.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: You shoot like the Lord's own sister. Who in hell are you?

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Somebody with a needle and thread, if you'll hold still. Who shot you?

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Syndicate's range detectives. They ran off my crew and kept the cattle. Hap Lindqvist. Was a drover. Am a hole, presently.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Ruth. The man who sent them. Eben Shale?

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: You know him? Then I'm sorry for you, Ruth. He's the kind smiles while he does it.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: We'll camp here tonight. Willow Bend's as good as anywhere, and you're not going anywhere.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Afternoon.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Ma'am.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Don't believe I know you.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: She's got a gun! Somebody fetch the sheriff!

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Lord, they're shooting!

lines.speaker: gunman
lines.line: There she is! Put her down!

lines.speaker: gunman
lines.line: Flank her, Lafe, go left!

lines.speaker: gunman
lines.line: I'm hit! God, I'm hit!

lines.speaker: gunman
lines.line: All right! All right, I'm done, don't shoot!

lines.speaker: bartender
lines.line: Whiskey's a dime, beer's a nickel, and conversation costs extra.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Then I'll buy the whiskey and you can throw in a name. Arliss Doane.

lines.speaker: bartender
lines.line: Arliss. Now there's a name nobody's asked after in two days. Since about the time they planted him.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Planted.

lines.speaker: bartender
lines.line: Up on Boot Hill, behind the church. Fell off his horse, the sheriff says. Fell on a bullet, some say quieter.

lines.speaker: gambler
lines.line: Lady's asking a lot of questions for somebody who hasn't sat down to cards.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Lady's watched you deal from the bottom twice. Wouldn't want my questions to get in the way of your business.

lines.speaker: mabry
lines.line: Ma'am. I'm told you've been asking after a dead man. Asking after dead men is how a person joins them, in this county.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: That a warning, Sheriff, or a confession?

lines.speaker: mabry
lines.line: It's advice. I give it free because nobody ever takes it. Doane drank, Doane rode, Doane fell. That's the inquest.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Who paid for the inquest?

lines.speaker: mabry
lines.line: ...Enjoy your stay in Bitter Spring, Mrs. Caddell. Keep it short.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Two days old. Somebody's cleaning house ahead of me, Tom.

lines.speaker: greer
lines.line: Everything a body needs and some things it shouldn't want. What'll it be?

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: The Shale brothers. Where they sleep, where they drink, who brings them their mail.

lines.speaker: greer
lines.line: Information's a dear commodity this far from the railroad. Twenty dollars dear.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Here's five, and the rest of my patience.

lines.speaker: greer
lines.line: Cutter Shale keeps a line camp up the Dry Fork. Eben's in Port Linden, wearing a necktie. That's free advice: don't go up the Dry Fork.

lines.speaker: shale_man
lines.line: That's her! Greer said she'd come this way!

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Five dollars for directions and a free ambush. Greer gives fair value.

lines.speaker: survivor
lines.line: Don't. Please. I just hold horses. Mr. Cutter pays a dollar a day.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Then go home and tell Mr. Cutter the price of a dollar just went up.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Smell that? That's not my coffee burning.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Get down. Stay by the wagon. Can you shoot?

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Better than I can run, presently.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Lady! They're cutting the horses loose! I seen 'em from the willows!

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Who in God's name are you?

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Billy! Billy Pruitt! I can catch horses, I'm good at horses!

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Then go catch them. Keep your head low.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: You could ride on, you know. Nobody'd blame you. I sure wouldn't.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I've been riding on for eighteen months. Turns out it's not much of a plan.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: We stay. We rebuild the camp, and in the morning we find out who sent them.
